title: Paper Towels 6-roll

drivers.name: 20% off promotion
drivers.evidence: Noise-adjusted lift from 18 past 20% off promotions is x2.09; this price drop is 16.4% vs regular (similar to past 20% off), deeper than 20% off but less than 30% off; historical 30% off events show higher lifts (x2.1–x3.3), but not in the same context. Lift is shrunk toward x2.0 due to lower depth

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 96.6. Halloween historically has no consistent impact (noise-adjusted x1.0), so no adjustment. The 20% off promotion has strong past lift (noise-adjusted x2.09), but the price drop is deeper (16.4% vs regular) than past 20% off events (20% off), and the 30% off events averaged x2.1–x3.3. The 2026-08-24 back-to-school 30% off week saw x3.32, but that was a seasonal ramp. This promotion is less deep and not in a season, so we shrink lift toward x2.0. The classical model suggests x2.09, which is close. No double-counting. The promotion is the only driver. Spread remains 1.0 unless uncertainty is high—here, evidence is strong (18 events), so no spread change. Confidence is high.

brief:
PRODUCT: Paper Towels 6-roll | category Household | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-10-26 to 2026-11-01 (3 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: Holiday: Halloween (Sat); Promotion: 20% off
  shelf price: 8.26 (-16.4% vs regular price 9.88)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 96.6 | 5%-95%: 62.8 - 233.5 | 10%-90%: 67.3 - 191.4

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-23% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
